subs.text: Scene three.
The Stranger Describes Odysseus.
In Crete they called me Aethon, third son of Deucalion, of the line of Minos.
Your husband was driven to my shore by a north wind, and I gave him bread and dark wine for twelve days.
Odysseus describes the king's purple cloak, golden brooch, tunic, and herald Eurybates in exact detail.
Penelope weeps as if melting snow while Odysseus keeps his eyes hard despite inward grief.
The stranger truly encountered her husband.
I swear:
swears Odysseus is near and will return within the month.

Eurycleia, rise and wash the feet of your master's age-mate.
By now the hands and feet of Odysseus must be worn as this man's are, if he is still under the sun.
Odysseus recognizes the danger but cannot refuse without suspicion.

subs.text: Scene five.
The Boar Hunt on Parnassus.
The scar triggers the story of young Odysseus visiting his grandfather Autolycus.
At dawn he hunts with his uncles on Mount Parnassus.
A boar bursts from dense cover and charges.
Odysseus spears it but receives a deep tusk wound above the knee.
The hunters bind the wound, stop the blood with a charm, and carry him home.

subs.text: Scene six.
The Dream of the Geese.
After the secret is restored, I tells the beggar your dream of twenty geese killed by a great eagle.
In the dream the eagle speaks with Odysseus's voice and says the geese are the suitors.
There is no second reading of it, lady.
The dream has told you its own meaning, and it has named the day of their death.
Announces the bow contest:
she will marry the man who strings Odysseus's bow and shoots through twelve axes.
Withdraws upstairs and Athena gives her sleep.

sign.operation: Dissolve into the dream, double exposure: twenty geese, the eagle, the voice of Odysseus.

scenes.world: a dim stone banquet hall with timber roof beams, lit only by hearth fire and oil lamps, silent-era costume drama look; late night, embers low, the dream intercut as soft double exposure of outdoor sky and water.

captain.asks: Dissolve into the dream as double exposure: geese, eagle, and the voice, then back to the hall and sleep.
diagnosis: Geese and a hawk give the dream real images; the double exposure the sign wants never happens.
Penelope is three different modern women across the scene; the hall is wallpaper and doorframes.
The ending works: a stair, then a bed.
